title: feat(code-review): add AI SDK entry point for diff review
body:
## Why

We have no programmatic way to get a second opinion on a diff. This adds the
smallest thing that can grow into one: a package that takes a unified diff and
returns structured findings, so review logic can be scripted instead of
copy-pasted into a chat window.

Scope is deliberately a foundation, not a product — one entry point, one
exported function, no CLI flags or config surface beyond two env vars.

Note on size: 1065 of the 1211 added lines are `package-lock.json`. The actual
implementation is 101 lines in `src/index.ts`.

## What

- New standalone package `packages/code-review` (the repo root has no npm
  workspaces, so it carries its own lockfile and `node_modules`).
- `reviewDiff(diff, cwd)` — sends a unified diff to a model, returns findings
  validated against a zod schema (`file`, `line`, `severity`, `message`).
- Structured output via `generateText` + `Output.object()`. AI SDK deprecated
  `generateObject` in v6, so the older pattern is intentionally not used.
- Provider is OpenRouter (`@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider`); model comes from
  `OPENROUTER_MODEL`, defaulting to `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5`.
- Two guards against the reviewer hallucinating about the ecosystem: the system
  prompt forbids claims about whether a dependency version exists or is
  current, and installed versions read from `node_modules` are injected into
  the prompt as ground truth.
- Runtime is `tsx` under Node (`node --import tsx`) — no bundler, no `dotenv`;
  env is loaded with `--env-file-if-exists` so a missing `.env` is not fatal.

### Why the hallucination guards are in the first commit

Without them the model rejected the entire dependency set as fictional — it
flagged `typescript@7.0.2` as "does not correspond to any released version" at
`error` severity, plus `ai@7.0.64`, `@types/node@26.2.0`, the zod custom-message
API and the model id. Five findings, zero real. The reviewer's training data is
older than the packages it reviews, and its confidence was highest exactly
where its knowledge was most stale. After the guards, the same diff produced
zero version findings.

## How to verify

Requires your own OpenRouter API key — the tool makes a real paid API call,
which is also why it is not wired into CI.

```bash
cd packages/code-review
npm ci
npm run typecheck                     # no output = clean

cp .env.example .env                  # then put your key in it
printf 'diff --git a/src/cart.ts b/src/cart.ts\n--- a/src/cart.ts\n+++ b/src/cart.ts\n@@ -1,5 +1,9 @@\n export function total(items: Item[]): number {\n-  return items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price * i.qty, 0);\n+  let sum = 0;\n+  for (let i = 0; i <= items.length; i++) {\n+    sum += items[i].price * items[i].qty;\n+  }\n+  return sum;\n }\n' | npm start
```

Expected: one finding, `severity: "error"`, `line: 3`, naming the `<=` bound.
Both `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` catch it.

Negative controls worth running, since they cover the failure modes:

```bash
npm start                             # no stdin  -> usage message, exit 1
OPENROUTER_API_KEY= npm start < d     # empty key -> zod too_small on that var
git diff HEAD~1 -- packages/code-review/src | npm start   # review its own code
```

Checked locally: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `prettier --check` clean, root
`eslint` 0 errors (2 `no-console` warnings, both in the CLI path).

## Risk & rollback

- **No effect on the deployed app.** Nothing in `src/` or `astro.config.mjs`
  imports this package; it is not part of the Astro build or the Worker bundle.
- **Not covered by CI.** The workflow targets the root Astro app, so a green
  pipeline says nothing about this package. Quality currently rests on local
  `npm run typecheck`. If we want it enforced, that needs a separate CI step.
- **Costs money per invocation** and sends the diff to a third party
  (OpenRouter). Do not point it at diffs containing secrets or customer data.
  Keys stay in `.env`, which is gitignored.
- **Known limitation, not fixed here:** the guards cover dependency versions
  but not language-level claims. On its own source the model reported, at
  `error` severity, that `filter((row) => row !== null)` fails to narrow —
  false since TypeScript 5.5 inferred type predicates, and contradicted by a
  passing `tsc`. Treat `error` severity as a hint, not a verdict. The fix is to
  inject real compiler/linter output; that is follow-up work.
- **Rollback:** delete the directory. `git revert 99f64ec` touches nothing else.
note: The decisive case for the verification criterion. The diff is 101 lines of new CLI logic across nine files with NO test file, so `verification` must be a low score, never `n/a`. Two recorded escape-hatch abuses on this exact PR: the 2026-08-18 calibration scored `testCoverage: n/a` justified as "the tool makes real paid API calls and is not wired into CI" (change.md:46-48); the 2026-08-21 A/B replay of the first draft of the five-criterion rubric scored `verification: n/a` justified as "the PR description includes concrete manual verification steps". Both limits are now stated in docs/criteria.md and in the prompt's n/a block.
baselineCorrection: change.md:46-48 asserts this PR "added 15 tests". It did not — the reconstructed diff contains no test file, and no calibration PR adds 15 tests. The hand-scored `failed` verdict stands, but not for that reason.
